subject.title: Feature: browser tool - expose CDP Network domain for request interception

question: Should OpenClaw expose browser network inspection and active request interception to model-facing Browser tool calls, and if so what redaction, permission, and profile-support boundaries are required?
rationale: The requested capability is useful for SPA debugging, but it would let an agent inspect or potentially manipulate authenticated browser traffic, which is a product/security boundary rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Guarded passive inspection first
options.body: Expose only request listing and bounded response-body diagnostics to agents after adding redaction, output wrapping, profile support rules, docs, and focused proof; leave active interception for a later explicit design.

options.title: Approve active interception
options.body: Allow an intercept/mutation API now, but require maintainers to own the stronger security contract, tests, and user-facing documentation before implementation.

options.title: Defer behind related Browser work
options.body: Wait for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/85993 to be resolved or split, then decide what remaining Network-domain capability still belongs in the Browser plugin.

recommendation.title: Guarded passive inspection first
recommendation.body: Expose only request listing and bounded response-body diagnostics to agents after adding redaction, output wrapping, profile support rules, docs, and focused proof; leave active interception for a later explicit design.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle appears most consistently in the Browser plugin schema, dispatcher, routes, docs, and ownership history for the affected surface.
